properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean strata of Lower Carboniferous sandstone and siltstone (Inverclyde and Strathclyde Groups) overlain by compacted glacial lodgement till. Primary structural masonry comprises fine-grained, pale buff-to-grey quartz-arenite sandstone quarried from local Craigleith and Hailes deposits. Bedding courses bound with traditional hydraulic lime and sharp silica sand mortars.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Mature urban parkland specimens of *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore) and *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime). December winter phenology: completely defoliated, displaying bare dendritic branch architectures, exposed dark bark trunks, dormant terminal buds, and dormant *Lolium perenne* turf groundcover.

properties.architectural_summary: Neoclassical urban square composition dominated by West Register House (formerly St George's Church). Central monument features a monumental tetrastyle portico, engaged giant order colonnade, square clock-stage attic, and a tiered cylindrical drum supporting a ribbed hemispherical dome with terminal cupola lantern. Flanking Robert Adam-designed terraces form unified multi-bay, three-storey compositions over rusticated basements, featuring planar ashlar facades, string courses, mutule cornices, continuous balustraded parapets, regular 6-over-6 timber sash-and-case fenestration, and steep slate mansards with robust chimney stacks. Central foreground retains the multi-tiered Prince Albert equestrian monument.
